best.plan_strategy: Attempt 2 stays on the ranking axis, which is where the residual is (cut_headroom 0.04463 vs a 0.0545 shortfall), and attacks the 0.1509 train-val gap with a regularised, lower-capacity, longer boosting run: hist_gbdt at learning_rate 0.03, max_iter 900, max_leaf_nodes 31, max_depth 6, min_samples_leaf 40, l2_regularization 10.0, early_stopping false so all 27,126 train rows are fitted. Keep the imbalance lever essentially where it was but nudge it up slightly (class_weight {\"0\": 1, \"1\": 7}) because recall 0.7382 still trails specificity 0.9150, while noting that lever is bounded by the reported headroom. Preprocessing unchanged: impute none (hist_gbdt splits on NaN natively; no NaNs present), no scaling, no missingness columns — the caveats' 'unknown' markers are ordinary one-hot levels here, not NaNs, so the missingness columns would be constant-zero and buy nothing. Read roc_auc / balanced_accuracy_at_best_cut against attempt 1's 0.9308 / 0.8712: if the regularised fit raises the at-best-cut ranking above 0.8811 the remaining work is the weight; if the ranking does not move, attempt 3 switches family (xgboost with column/row subsampling, or random_forest) rather than re-tuning inside this one.

critic.evidence: Attempt 1 (hist_gbdt, lr 0.06, 500 iters, 63 leaves, l2 1.0, class_weight 1:6) scored balanced_accuracy 0.8266 (95% CI 0.8135–0.8391) against the bar 0.8811 — a shortfall of 0.0545, and the whole CI sits below the bar. Train balanced_accuracy is 0.9775 versus 0.8266 on validation, train_val_gap 0.1509, with train_f1 0.8621 against val f1 0.6203: the fit is deep into memorisation territory. On the operating-point axis, cut_headroom is only 0.04463 (balanced_accuracy_at_best_cut 0.8712, i.e. KS 0.7424 versus the required 0.7622), so even a perfectly placed cut of this ranking still lands 0.0099 short of 0.8811 — the residual is in the ranking. recall 0.7382 is below specificity 0.9150, so the 1:6 weight is still slightly under-weighted, but that lever is bounded by the 0.04463 headroom and cannot close the gap alone. No hyperparameters were dropped (dropped_hyperparams empty), train_time 10.8 s of a 600 s budget, so there is ample room to spend on more iterations at a lower learning rate. Only one family has been tried (1 run, best 0.8266), so 'families have plateaued' is not yet established — the regularisation/capacity setting inside this family is untested.
critic.direction: Stay on the ranking axis but move a single lever: refit hist_gbdt with the same 1:6 class weight and same preprocessing while cutting capacity per tree and adding regularisation (max_leaf_nodes 31, l2_regularization 5.0, min_samples_leaf 40, max_iter 800 at learning_rate 0.04), since the 0.1509 train-val gap says the current 63-leaf/500-iter fit is memorising rather than ranking, and only ~0.010 of the 0.0545 shortfall can come from the cut.

critic.evidence: Attempt 2 (hist_gbdt, lr 0.03, 900 iters, 31 leaves, depth 6, min_samples_leaf 40, l2 10.0, class_weight 1:7) scored balanced_accuracy 0.8624 (95% CI 0.8510–0.8737) against the bar 0.8811 — the whole CI sits below the bar, shortfall 0.0187. The regularisation prescription paid: paired Δ vs iteration 1 is +0.0358 (95% CI +0.0266~+0.0449, P(better) 1.000, resolved), train_val_gap fell 0.1509→0.0584 and train_balanced_accuracy 0.9775→0.9208, so memorisation is no longer the binding constraint and the overfitting diagnosis is now spent. The residual is on the ranking axis: cut_headroom collapsed 0.04463→0.012313 (balanced_accuracy_at_best_cut 0.8747, i.e. KS 0.7494 vs the required 0.7622), so even a perfectly placed cut of this ranking still lands 0.0064 short of 0.8811, and recall 0.8488 now slightly exceeds specificity 0.8760 — the 1:7 weight is essentially at the crossing, bracketing the optimum between 1:6 (recall 0.7382 < specificity 0.9150) and 1:7, so the weight lever has ~0.012 left at most and cannot cover the 0.0187. The ledger sizes this the same way: cut_headroom 0.0123 vs 0.0187 remaining means 34% of the distance is ranking that no decision rule reaches. Only one family has been tried (hist_gbdt, 2 runs, best 0.8624), so 'families plateaued' is not yet established and no ranking-ceiling spread over families exists to argue against a swap; roc_auc moved 0.9308→0.9351 within the family while the at-best-cut ranking moved only 0.8712→0.8747. No hyperparameters were dropped, train_time 14.9 s of a 600 s budget. calibration_error rose 0.0487→0.1057 and brier 0.0743→0.0889, consistent with the heavier positive weight, but neither is targetable.
critic.direction: Switch family to xgboost with column and row subsampling under the identical impute:none / no-scale / no-missingness pipeline — the ranking, not the cut, holds the last 0.0064–0.0187 (cut_headroom 0.0123, at-best-cut 0.8747 vs bar 0.8811), and a different tree-growing and feature-sampling scheme is the only untried lever on that axis; keep the imbalance setting at the measured crossing (scale_pos_weight 7, recall 0.8488 vs specificity 0.8760) so this transition moves exactly one lever and stays attributable.

critic.evidence: Attempt 3 (xgboost, scale_pos_weight 7, identical impute:none pipeline) scored balanced_accuracy 0.8423 (95% CI 0.8287–0.8534), a paired -0.0201 vs attempt 2 (CI -0.0288~-0.0117, P(better) 0.000 — resolved), so the family swap I prescribed last time is refuted, not unresolved: it moved the ranking the wrong way (balanced_accuracy_at_best_cut 0.8747→0.8687, roc_auc 0.9351→0.9316). It also failed to stop: internal_validation shows stopped_at_iter 1500 = max_iter 1500, and train_val_gap rose 0.0584→0.1062 with train_balanced_accuracy 0.9484 — 1500 unstopped trees on 24,413 fit rows re-introduced the memorisation attempt 2 had removed, i.e. the settings, not the estimator, are the visible fault in this row. That is what is different from my previous wrong_model_family verdict, and it is also why another family off the same list is not the plan: the two families tried span balanced_accuracy_at_best_cut 0.8687–0.8747 (width 0.0060), while even a perfectly placed cut of the current best still lands 0.0064 short of 0.8811 (KS 0.7494 vs required 0.7622) — the shortfall is the full width of everything the swap axis has bought, and the ledger's own family-swap sizes are 0.0022–0.0077 roc_auc against a paired resolution of 0.003–0.006. On the operating-point axis this attempt still has recall 0.7826 below specificity 0.9019 (under-weighted at 1:7 for xgboost) with cut_headroom 0.0264 against 0.0388 remaining, so at most 68% of the distance is buyable there and only from a ranking at least as good as attempt 2's. No hyperparameters were dropped; 13.8 s of 600 s used, so cost is not binding. Two iterations remain.
